other_up.note:
Restrict to a set $S$ with $|S| = d = \deg_2(f)$ carrying a top $\mathbb{F}_2$-monomial.
The restriction $g$ (as a $0/1$-valued function on $d$ bits) still contains
$\prod_{i\in S} x_i$, so $\sum_x g(x)$ is odd. For the $\pm1$ encoding
$h = 1-2g$ and any $T\ne\emptyset$,
$\hat h(T) = -2^{1-d}\sum_x g(x)\chi_T(x)$, and $\sum_x g(x)\chi_T(x) \equiv \sum_x g(x)
\pmod 2$ is odd, hence nonzero. So all $2^d-1$ non-empty coefficients survive, and
restriction never increases sparsity. The $+1$ is not slack: $\oplus_n$ has
$\deg_2 = 1$ and $\mathrm{spar} = 1$, so the bound is attained.

other_lo.note: Attained again at the other end: $\mathrm{spar}(\mathrm{OR}_n) = 2^n$ and the $\mathbb{F}_2$-polynomial of $\mathrm{OR}_n$ contains $x_1\cdots x_n$.

Upper bounds — holds for every total

  • \(\deg_2(f) \le \log_2\big(\mathrm{spar}(f)+1\big)\)
    putative
    Restrict to a set $S$ with $|S| = d = \deg_2(f)$ carrying a top $\mathbb{F}_2$-monomial. The restriction $g$ (as a $0/1$-valued function on $d$ bits) still contains $\prod_{i\in S} x_i$, so $\sum_x g(x)$ is odd. For the $\pm1$ encoding $h = 1-2g$ and any $T\ne\emptyset$, $\hat h(T) = -2^{1-d}\sum_x g(x)\chi_T(x)$, and $\sum_x g(x)\chi_T(x) \equiv \sum_x g(x) \pmod 2$ is odd, hence nonzero. So all $2^d-1$ non-empty coefficients survive, and restriction never increases sparsity. The $+1$ is not slack: $\oplus_n$ has $\deg_2 = 1$ and $\mathrm{spar} = 1$, so the bound is attained.
